'''''Lythrum hyssopifolia''''' ({{abbr|[[orthographical variant|orth. var.]]|Orthographical variant}} ''L. hyssopifolium'') is a species of flowering plant in the [[Lythraceae|loosestrife family]] known by the common names '''hyssop loosestrife'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=LYHY3|taxon=Lythrum hyssopifolium|accessdate=27 January 2016}}</ref> and '''grass-poly'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> It is native to Europe but it is known elsewhere, including parts of Australia and eastern and western North America, as an [[introduced species]] and sometimes a [[noxious weed|weed]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cdfa.ca.gov/phpps/ipc/weedinfo/lythrum.htm |publisher=California Dept. of Food & Agriculture |title=''Lythrum''|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703083241/http://www.cdfa.ca.gov/phpps/ipc/weedinfo/lythrum.htm|archive-date=3 July 2009}}</ref> It is rare in the United Kingdom, with occasional isolated populations.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-55104153 |title=Surprise discovery of rare plant at Norfolk 'ghost pond' |author=Helen Briggs |publisher=BBC |date=28 November 2020 |accessdate=28 November 2020}}</ref> It often grows in moist habitats, such as [[marsh]]es and wet agricultural fields, [[paddy field|rice paddies]], for example.

It is a mostly upright, branching annual or biennial herb growing {{convert|10 to 60|cm|in|sp=us}} tall. The oval leaves are arranged oppositely lower on the plant, and often alternately toward the top. They are up to {{convert|3|cm|in|sp=us}} in length. The [[inflorescence]] is a terminal spike of flowers with pinkish petals up to half a centimeter (¼") long. The fruit is an oval capsule containing many minute seeds.

The Latin word ''hyssopifolia'' (which occurs in several plant names) means "[[hyssopus officinalis|hyssop]]-leafed".<ref>{{cite book|author=James Donn|author-link=James Donn |title=''Hortus Cantabrigiensis'': or, a Catalogue of Plants, Indigenous and Exotic |year=1809 |page= 5}}</ref>
